newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans cleared in online child torture case.
newsitem.headline: Germans cleared in online child torture case.

text.p: A couple who offered children as slaves for sadistic sex via a computer online service walked free on Tuesday after a German court cleared them of conspiracy to abuse, kidnap and murder.
Presiding judge Peter Froehlich said prosecutors had not been able to remove the doubt over whether the couple were serious when they offered Czech girls as "young slaves".
Bernd Malitzki and Sabine Pohl-Jovanovic, a couple in their thirties, had told the court in the Bavarian town of Traunstein that their offers were not serious.

Prosecutors, who had demanded long jail sentences for both the accused, had also alleged that the couple said in a telephone call to a journalist posing a client that they would dispose of a child's corpse for 3,000 marks ($1,600).
Police had found a torture chamber in the couple's home along with indications of sado-masochistic activity, but they discovered no evidence of child abuse.
